$comment: What logix-core is made of: each tool's pinned upstream release (or, for a tool upstream publishes no build of, its pinned upstream source, which logix-core builds unmodified: build, with platforms naming the only platforms that have it): files, URL and run folders per platform (path: the PATH folders, relative to the component, the first holding its programs; ../ reaches another component; env: variables naming folders, relative to the component, per platform where needed), or one value for every platform (elkjs). Changed only by pull request (docs/design.md, Processes). scripts/build.py reads it. Boards aren't here: they're the logix-catalog package. The list of FPGAs the tools can build is generated from their databases (scripts/fpgas.py).

oss-cad-suite.description: YosysHQ OSS CAD Suite: yosys, nextpnr, icestorm, Project Trellis, Apycula, Icarus Verilog, Verilator, GTKWave, openFPGALoader and more

openxc7.description: openXC7: nextpnr-xilinx, the Project X-Ray tools and database, for Xilinx 7-series FPGAs

verible.description: CHIPS Alliance Verible: the Verilog formatter and language server

elkjs.description: ELK (the Eclipse Layout Kernel) for JavaScript: lays out Logix Engine's design diagrams, run by the engine itself

wdi-simple.description: libwdi's wdi-simple: installs the WinUSB driver for a USB device, which Logix Engine runs on Windows to set up boards. libwdi publishes no build of it, so logix-core builds it from the pinned libwdi source, unmodified (scripts/build-wdi-simple.sh)

wdk.$comment: Microsoft's WDF co-installers, which libwdi embeds for WinUSB: the file go.microsoft.com/fwlink/p/?LinkID=253170 leads to, pinned by its SHA-256
